document_title: Hampton University and Subsidiaries, Consolidated Financial Statements, June 30, 2024 and 2023 (With Independent Auditors' Reports Thereon) [FY2024 single audit package, FAC report 2024-06-GSAFAC-0000363434]
quote: Consolidated Statements of Financial Position, June 30, 2024: "Notes payable (note 9) 29,425,586"; "Bonds payable, net (note 8) 101,120,368". Note 8: "Total bonds payable 97,751,236"; "Plus unamortized bond issuance premiums 4,005,746"; "Less unamortized debt issuance costs, net (636,614)"; "Bonds payable, net $ 101,120,368". Note 9 maturities total "$ 29,425,586".
arithmetic: bonds_payable 101,120,368 (net carrying value = principal 97,751,236 + premium 4,005,746 - issuance costs 636,614) + notes_loans_mortgages_payable 29,425,586 + finance_lease_obligations 0 = 130,545,954. Statements are in whole dollars. No finance lease liability and no line of credit appear on the balance sheet or in the notes.
reporting_entity: Hampton University and Subsidiaries (consolidated; includes 27th Street Hotel, LLC, 58.7% owned, acquired June 2024)
caveats: IPEDS $0 is a reporting gap: the audited statements show $130.5 million. (1) Bonds payable is carried net of unamortized debt issuance costs (636,614) and includes premium (4,005,746); principal outstanding is 97,751,236. It includes a Historically Black Colleges and Universities Capital Financing Loan Agreement 'Future Advance Project Funding Bond, Series A 2024-1' of 12,896,236 issued in FY2024 (maximum 91,500,000); note 1(r) reports a further 13,230,623 of advances after year end. (2) Notes payable of 29,425,586 includes notes of the newly consolidated hotel subsidiary assumed in June 2024: a senior NONRECOURSE note (note 9 text: balance 21,972,952) and a 2,500,000 junior unsecured note. Note 16 records 'Notes payables 24,500,000' assumed. Excluding the hotel notes at 24,500,000, University-level long-term debt would be 106,045,954. The individual balances stated in the note 9 text (4,414,235 + 511,351 + 21,972,952 + 2,500,000 = 29,398,538) are 27,048 lower than the balance sheet and maturity-table total of 29,425,586; the balance sheet figure is used. (3) During FY2024 the 2015 VCBA series was paid off and a multifamily note (4,155,117) was paid off by the HBCU Capital Financing Program on June 28, 2024. (4) Excluded: 'Loans refundable' 787,234 (federal Perkins advances), 'Other liabilities' 2,584,998, deferred revenue; hotel ground-lease liabilities stated to be not material. No going-concern paragraph.
form_990_crosscheck: Form 990 summary data (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API, tax period 2024-06; not audited, cross-check only): tax-exempt bond liabilities 101,120,368; secured mortgages and notes payable 29,425,586; total liabilities 185,568,677. Agrees with the audited statements.

document_title: Livingstone College, Financial Statements as of June 30, 2024 and 2023 Together With Independent Auditor's Report [FAC report 2024-06-GSAFAC-0000056817]
page: 6 (balance sheet); 19 (note 6); 20 (note 7); 21-23 (note 8; tables are images, read from the rendered page); 28 (note 12); 30-31 (note 13)
quote: Statements of Financial Position, 2024 Total: "Finance lease liability - current portion 1,611,786"; "Notes payable - current portion 2,512,362"; "Finance lease liability 556,339"; "Notes payable 70,466". Note 6: "On November 29, 2023, the College entered into a $2,500,000 variable rate revolving credit ... The advances totaled $2,500,000 as of June 30, 2024." Note 7: "$94,000 Automobile installment loan ... 82,828"; "Total notes payable $ 82,828". Note 8: "Total lease obligations, net $ 2,168,125".
arithmetic: notes_loans_mortgages_payable 82,828 (automobile loan: 12,362 current + 70,466 noncurrent) + finance_lease_obligations 2,168,125 (1,611,786 current + 556,339 noncurrent) + bonds_payable 0 = 2,250,953. The balance sheet 'Notes payable' lines total 2,582,828 (2,512,362 + 70,466) because the 2,500,000 revolving line of credit is included in 'Notes payable - current portion'; that 2,500,000 is reported separately as a short-term line of credit and NOT included. Check: 2,250,953 + 2,500,000 = 4,750,953 = 'Total Debt at June 30, 2024' in note 13. Statements are in whole dollars.
caveats: IPEDS $0 is a reporting gap, though the amount is small. Note 7 is titled 'Notes and Bonds Payable' but lists only the automobile loan; there are no bonds. Finance leases comprise a master lease for a turf field and scoreboard (1,834,476 at June 30, 2024) and vehicle/office-equipment leases (333,649). Note 12: a 1.2 million balloon payment on the turf-field lease was due July 2024 and the lease was modified on September 27, 2024; the 2,500,000 line of credit matured February 2025 and its renewal date was extended 90 days to May 29, 2025. If the fully drawn line of credit were counted, total borrowings would be 4,750,953. Presentation inconsistencies in the document that do not affect the debt figures: the cash flow statement heading reads 'years ended June 30, 2023 and 2022' while the columns are 2024 and 2023; the ED schedule on p.33 shows total assets of 100,159,198 versus 100,144,198 on the balance sheet; the note 13 table on p.31 labels the 2,500,000 as 'Capital leases' and is captioned 'Total debt at June 30, 2023'. Accounts payable and accrued expenses rose to 12,079,436. The auditor's report has an emphasis-of-matter paragraph on lease accounting only; no going-concern paragraph. The note 7 and note 8 tables are embedded images and were read from the rendered page; they reconcile to the balance sheet text.
